title: Closed support triangle adds one to the Tor upper bound
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow T$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small étale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $i^\times$ be right adjoint to $i_*$, as in [lem-exc-closed-ambient], and suppose $i_*$ and $i^*$ are exact and the counit $i^*i_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is an isomorphism. Let $a\le b$ be integers, $e\ge0$ an integer, and $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Put $Q=Rj_*j^*K$ and suppose that $Q$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+e]$ and that
$$ i_*i^\times K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow(i_*i^\times K)[1] $$
is the distinguished closed-support triangle. Then $i^\times K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+e+1]$ on $Z$.

source.place: Step 3, support triangle and long-exact-sequence argument giving the extra +1 in the upper Tor endpoint.

proof.text: Put $E=i^\times K$ and $F=i_*E$. The exact functors $i_*$ and $i^*$ act termwise on derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. If $C^\bullet$ represents $E$, the natural counit maps $i^*i_*C^r\to C^r$ commute with the differentials and are isomorphisms by hypothesis. They give an isomorphism $i^*F\simeq E$. For an arbitrary $A_Z$-module sheaf $N$, put $M=i_*N$, a degree-zero $A_T$-module sheaf. The same counit gives $i^*(M[0])\simeq N[0]$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, termwise exact functors; apply the hypothesized counit in each degree.

proof.text: Fix the arbitrary sheaf $N$ and its direct image $M$ from step 1. Apply the triangulated functor $-\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M[0]$ of [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated] to the distinguished triangle assumed in the statement. This gives a distinguished triangle with vertices $F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M$, $K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M$, $Q\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M$. By [def-kun-tor-amplitude] and the two given Tor bounds, the second vertex has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ and the third only in $[a,b+e]$. No flatness of $M$ is required because the tensor product is derived.

source.place: Tags 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor); tensor the support triangle in the blueprint closed-immersion paragraph.

proof.text:
For every integer $r$, [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the exact segment
$$H^{r-1}(Q\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M)\longrightarrow H^r(F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M)\longrightarrow H^r(K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M).$$
If $r<a$, then $r-1<a$ and $r<a$, so both outer terms vanish. If $r>b+e+1$, then $r-1>b+e$ and $r>b$ since $e\geq0$, so both outer terms again vanish. Exactness therefore gives $H^r(F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M)=0$ for every $r\notin[a,b+e+1]$. This proves the extra $+1$ directly at the required degrees.

source.place: Tags 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological) and 0147 (definition-homological), equation-long-exact-cohomology-sequence; the blueprint closed-support Tor-interval argument.

proof.text: Apply the cohomology comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] to the exact functor $i^*$ and the object $F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M$. Its statement gives $H^r(i^*(F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M))\simeq i^*H^r(F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M)$ for every integer $r$ and every derived object; despite the node's title, this clause has no bounded-below hypothesis. For $r\notin[a,b+e+1]$ the right side is $i^*(0)=0$, by step 3 and exactness. Thus $i^*(F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M)$ has cohomology only in that interval.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), applied termwise; homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor) gives the kernel and image comparison.

proof.text:
The inverse of the monoidal comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], applied to the scheme morphism $i$ and the commutative coefficient ring $A$, and then the two counit isomorphisms of step 1 give
$$i^*(F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M)\simeq i^*F\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}i^*M\simeq E\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}N.$$
Consequently step 4 says that $H^r(E\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}N)=0$ for every $r\notin[a,b+e+1]$. The sheaf $N$ on $Z$ was arbitrary, so [def-kun-tor-amplitude] gives exactly the claimed Tor amplitude for $E=i^\times K$.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); the counit identifications use the exact inverse image of step 1.
